title: Cross-delay frozen-state linear readout transfer
research_question: Does a delay8-fitted prior-answer linear readout lose more delay32 accuracy in the block model than the matched random model, relative to a delay32-fitted head?
strongest_rejection_reason: Probe transfer reflects an input/time distribution shift and its own fitting family; it cannot causally identify why the pretrained task head fails.
hypothesis: Difference-in-transfer-loss D=(H32A-H8A)_M3-(H32A-H8A)_C0 at delay32 is at least+5pp, with paired seed CI lower>+5pp and all guards passed.
intervention: Fit separate linear prior-answer probes at delay8 and32; apply both on identical frozen delay32 hidden states using common short-delay scaler
controls: behavioral gap and validation adequacy guards
independent H8B source refit and stability guard
dataset: Fresh original task streams 930000/935000/940000/950000+delay; unique paired prefixes; 4096/1024/2048 A-train/validation/test and 4096 B-train
resource_matching: M3/C0 model resources inherited EXP-0004; each probe260 coefficients, same normalization method and sample counts
interpretation: M3 has +8.91pp more fixed-ridge H8-to-32 transfer loss than C0; paired CI [+1.57,+15.78]pp supports direction but not a guaranteed minimum +5pp.
limitations: delay length and noise load change together
frozen probe family not original task head
next_action: STOP_MECHANISM_ESCALATION; retain fixed-probe transfer finding without Gate1 advancement.
